title: Sohila close
hookLine: five hymns to sleep on: praise, one sun, the sky's aarti, the city, now

lines: THE WORDS IN THE AIR: SOHILA.
cards: Every night in a gurdwara there's a quiet moment most visitors never see. The evening singing ends.
The Guru Granth Sahib, open since dawn, is closed, wrapped in cloth, and carried with care to its resting room, often lifted on someone's head while the sangat stands.
The ceremony is called sukhasan, the position of rest. And as the scripture goes to rest, the words in the air are Sohila. Two weeks ago we opened these five hymns.

teach.b: Here are the five, the way you might remember them lying in the dark. One, Guru Nanak: the house of praise. Jai ghar keerat: in the house where the Creator's praise is spoken and reflected on, sing.

And the wedding at its end: the date written, friends pouring oil at the door, the bride called. Two, Guru Nanak: six schools, six teachers, six teachings, one Guru of gurus in many forms; many seasons, one sun.

teach.h: TWO AND THREE: ONE SUN, THE SKY'S AARTI.
teach.b: Three, Guru Nanak: the sky's aarti. Gagan mai thaal: the sky the platter, sun and moon the lamps, the stars the pearls, the wind the fan, the forests the flowers.
Four, Guru Ram Das: the city. Kaam karodh: desire and anger crowd the body's streets, the thorn of ego pricks with every step, and meeting the holy breaks them up.
Five, Guru Arjan: now. Karau benantee: listen, friends, life runs down day and night; this is the time to serve; make me the dust of the holy's feet. Look at the movement.
A doorway, the calendar, the sky, back inside the body, then a friend leaning close.
Praise, unity, wonder, honesty, urgency. And then sleep.
That's the shape Sikhs lie down inside every night, and the same shape sung when a life is done: a whole evening, and a whole life, held between praise at the beginning and humility at the end.

how: Sikhs read or listen to Kirtan Sohila every night before sleep, and in gurdwaras it is recited as the Guru Granth Sahib is closed and carried to rest in the sukhasan ceremony.

o: a cushion where the sangat sits for kirtan
rest: the scripture laid down for the night
the morning ceremony that opens the scripture

games.q: Sohila's five hymns — tap the pairs.

s: Sohila is recited as the Guru Granth Sahib is laid to rest at night
the sukhasan ceremony, the position of rest.
all five hymns of Sohila are by one Guru
Guru Nanak wrote three, Guru Ram Das one, Guru Arjan one.
Guru Arjan asks to be the dust of the holy's feet.

games.q: the evening singing is over in the gurdwara, and the scripture has been open since dawn. what happens now?
o: it is left open all night.
it is closed and carried to rest while Sohila is recited.
it is read aloud from beginning to end.
games.why: at sukhasan the Guru Granth Sahib is wrapped and laid to rest, and the words in the air are Sohila.

practice: Walk through the five in your mind, the house, the sun, the sky, the city, the friend, and give each one a breath. On the last breath, picture the day being wrapped and laid to rest, like the scripture at sukhasan.
If you pray, say Waheguru once.

wordCard.voice: Sukhasan, the position of rest: as the Guru Granth Sahib is put to rest each night, Sohila is sung, five hymns by three Gurus said at bedtime and at the end of a life.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: sohila, the song of praise Sikhs sleep on.

carryVoice: Your line: sleep in praise. Praise first, humility last, and rest in between. Two weeks of Sohila, done.
